To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have prepared a new N(4)ethyl-N(4)-C interstrand crosslinking reagent that is suitable for the preparation of oligonucleotide duplexes containing interstrand cross-links, that the thermal stability of duplexes that contain this cross-link is significantly increased relative to the melting temperatures of duplexes that lack the cross-link, and that the orientation of the cross-link can have an important effect on the structure of the duplex and on the thermal stability of this structure.

1) the N(4) C-ethyl-N( 4)C cross-links stabilize DNA duplexes, and 2) duplexes with a staggered cross-link have a CD spectrum that is similar to B-form DNA, but the thermal stability of a duplex with a -GC- cross-link is reduced compared to that of a control duplex with a G-C pair.
we have synthesized and characterized short DNA duplexes containing a N(4)-ethyl-N(4)-C interstrand cross-links between C-C residues or between the C residues of -CG- or GC- steps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of DNA duplexes containing interstrand cross-links.
the synthesis, characterization and application of short oligonucleotides that contain site-specifically positioned and oriented interstrand cross-links.
the development of synthetic DNA molecules that are useful as substrates for the study of DNA repair and replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates that N(4)ethyl-N(4)-C interstrand cross-linked DNA is a versatile tool for probing the structural consequences of cross-linked DNA.
the cross-linked duplexes have been synthesized and characterized, and that the results obtained are consistent with the proposed structures.
the N(4) C-ethyl-N( 4) C phosphoramidite is a useful reagent for introducing a variety of interstrand cross-links into DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cross-link between two mismatched C-C base pairs stabilizes adjacent base pairings, whereas the staggered cross-linked -CG- or GC- steps perturb the structure and stability, and the -GC- step also appears to disrupt hydrogen bonding.

the N(4) C-ethyl-N( 4)C cross-link is a useful reagent for studying the effects of interstrand cross-links on duplex structure, but it does not appear to be an ideal substrate for studying DNA repair mechanisms.
the N(4) ethylation of the C residues in DNA leads to the formation of interstrand cross-links with different orientations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to prepare DNA duplexes with a variety of interstrand cross-links that have different orientations, which can be used as models for the study of DNA repair mechanisms.
the orientation of an N(4) ethyl cross-link can affect both the thermal stability of a duplex and the structure of the cross-linked helix.
the orientation and position of an interstrand crosslink can have a significant impact on the structure and physical properties of the cross-linked helix.
